main_text.p: Syllaba longa natura primó ex ꞑ, ω, & diphthongo: ut ἥρως heros, ἤνοος benevolus. deinde contracta quæli-bet, ἀργύρεα ἀργυρέα argentea, τοὺς ὄφι-ας ὄφις serpentes, δρῦς δρῦς quercus. tum é finalibus α & υ, sequente ρ: & ι, sequente ν: ut ὁ Κάρ Car, ὁ ἴαρ sturnus avis: ὁ πῦρ ignis, ὁ πίστρυρ testis: ἡμῖν nobis, ὑμῖν vobis. Longa positione, ut ἐλάμον digitis pulsabam.

Anceps, ut α, ι, υ, in καλὸς honestus, φίλος amicus, ὕδωρ aqua, φύω nascor: ubi produci potest & corripi, quales voces Hephæstioni enumerantur sexaginta sex, aliis Grammaticis multo plures. In quibusdam tantum longæ sunt, in quibusdam tantum breves, quales sunt longé plurimæ. ancipites tamen vulgò dicuntur secus

page.notes: Greek and polytonic forms are partly blurred by show-through and damage; several Greek words are uncertain and should be checked against the scan. The stray "b" below the text is printed; its status as a signature is doubtful.
